title: feat: add --width CLI argument and extra tests
description: This PR adds support for a new `--width` command-line option to the `multimark` CLI, allowing users to specify output wrapping for certain formats. It also add tests for this feature, as well as new tests for GFM-specific options, footnote and source position keyword arguments, and some edge cases in the renderers.

title: feat: add CLI
description: This PR introduces a new command-line interface, allowing users to convert Markdown files to various formats directly from the terminal. It adds the necessary CLI implementation (using Click), dependencies, packaging configuration, and tests.

title: feat: multimark parser and 3.14 + Pyodide wheels
description: This PR introduces a new streaming `Parser` class to the library. This enables incremental Markdown parsing and rendering. We also add full test coverage for the new parser, expand build and CI support (including Python 3.14 and Pyodide wheels), and expose additional C API bindings for tree traversal and node introspection.

title: Build Linux aarch64 wheels
description:
## Summary

- build manylinux and musllinux wheels for Linux aarch64
- set up QEMU in the release and manual wheel-build workflows
- document the expanded Linux wheel matrix

## Motivation

Linux aarch64 users currently fall back to building the source distribution because PyPI only contains Linux x86_64 wheels. This adds aarch64 to the existing cp39-abi3 builds so one wheel per Linux platform supports CPython 3.9 and newer.

## Validation

- `cibuildwheel==2.23.4 --platform linux --print-build-identifiers` includes:
  - `cp39-manylinux_aarch64`
  - `cp39-musllinux_aarch64`
- `6643 passed, 43 xfailed` on Python 3.14
- both edited GitHub Actions workflows parse as valid YAML

The QEMU setup follows cibuildwheel's documented approach for building non-native Linux architectures on GitHub Actions.

title: feat: batch API
description: This PR adds a fast batch rendering API for Markdown-to-HTML conversion, enabling multiple documents to be rendered efficiently in a single call. The main feature is the new `markdown_to_html_batch()` function, which leverages a C-level batch renderer to reduce Python overhead and allows for multi-threaded parallelism. The implementation includes C and Python bindings, and there are tests to ensure correctness and performance.
